title: PubChem Periodic Table
blurb: The first 96 elements, hydrogen to curium. One view is how they behave: electronegativity, size, ionization energy, electron affinity, melting and boiling points, density. The other is simply where each one sits on the 18-column periodic table (f-block rows underneath).

notes.neighbors: Columns keep their friends: francium’s nearest neighbors on properties alone are caesium, rubidium and potassium, astatine’s are iodine, tellurium and selenium. Periods do not: the table puts iron next to cobalt, and so do the properties, but carbon’s property neighbors are iridium, rhodium and nickel.

about.name: PubChem Periodic Table and Element pages
about.quote: Overall, the PubChem Periodic Table and Element pages improve access to chemical element data from authoritative sources.
about.label: PubChem team, Chemistry Teacher International

here: Here: hydrogen to curium (Z 1–96), as seven z-scored properties — electronegativity, atomic radius, ionization energy, electron affinity, and log melting point, boiling point and density (A) — and as row and column on the familiar 18-column table, with the f-block as two rows underneath and Lu under Y (B); blank electron affinities count as 0, He/Ne/Ar/Rn take Allen-scale electronegativities, and the last eight gaps are filled from each element's five nearest neighbours on the rest.

pubchem_ptable.text: Kim, S., Gindulyte, A., Zhang, J., Thiessen, P. A., Bolton, E. E. (2020). PubChem Periodic Table and Element pages: improving access to information on chemical elements from authoritative sources. Chemistry Teacher International 3(1), 57–65.
